common_name: Kramer's Beauty Camellia (Deep Red Peony-Form Camellia japonica)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade; Kramer's Beauty is a sport of the fragrant Kramer's Supreme camellia, sharing its deep red color and rich scent on a peony-form flower.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade with protection from harsh afternoon sun. Kramer's Beauty bears large, deep red, peony-form flowers and carries the same notable fragrance as its parent, Kramer's Supreme, an unusual trait since most camellias have little to no scent. The vigorous, upright evergreen shrub blooms in mid-season, providing dense, glossy year-round structure in addition to its fragrant winter flowers. Mulch heavily with pine bark or pine straw to maintain the acidic, evenly moist soil camellias need, and prune only to remove dead or crossing branches after bloom.

common_name: Tomorrow Camellia (Large Rose-Red Peony-Form Camellia japonica)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade; Tomorrow is a popular Southern camellia known for enormous, heavy peony-to-rose-form blooms and has produced several sport variants.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade with protection from harsh afternoon sun. Tomorrow bears enormous, heavy rose-red to deep pink blooms in a loose peony to rose form, among the largest flowers produced by any widely grown camellia japonica cultivar, and has given rise to several popular sports and color variants sold under related names. The vigorous, spreading evergreen shrub blooms in mid-to-late season and needs sturdy branching to support its oversized flowers. Mulch heavily with pine bark or pine straw to maintain the acidic, evenly moist soil camellias need, and prune only to remove dead or crossing branches after bloom.

common_name: C.M. Wilson Camellia (Light Pink Anemone-Form Camellia japonica)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade; C.M. Wilson is a classic Southern camellia bearing soft pink anemone-to-peony-form flowers.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade with protection from harsh afternoon sun. C.M. Wilson bears large, soft light-pink blooms in an anemone to loose peony form, with a mass of small petaloids at the center surrounded by broader outer petals, a classic old Southern camellia form that has remained popular for generations. The vigorous, upright evergreen shrub blooms over a long midseason window and provides dense, glossy year-round structure. Mulch heavily with pine bark or pine straw to maintain the acidic, evenly moist soil camellias need, and prune only to remove dead or crossing branches after bloom.

common_name: Guilio Nuccio Camellia (Large Coral-Pink Semi-Double Camellia japonica)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade; Guilio Nuccio, from California's renowned Nuccio's Nurseries, is one of the most celebrated camellia show cultivars ever introduced.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade with protection from harsh afternoon sun. Guilio Nuccio bears exceptionally large, coral-pink, semi-double flowers with broad, well-arranged petals and a striking cluster of golden stamens at the center, a cultivar bred by the famed Nuccio's Nurseries of California that has become one of the most award-winning and widely exhibited camellias in American show history. The vigorous, upright evergreen shrub blooms in mid-season and holds its flower form beautifully both on the plant and as a cut bloom. Mulch heavily with pine bark or pine straw to maintain the acidic, evenly moist soil camellias need, and prune only to remove dead or crossing branches after bloom.
